morphology.motility: Highly motile — multiple polar flagella (flagellar tuft)

habitat.hostAssociation: Chronic colonizer of the human stomach, found in a large proportion of the population worldwide, often asymptomatically
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Not a significant free-living environmental organism
habitat.reservoir: Human stomach; transmission is likely person to person

microscopy.stain: Gram stain or silver stain of gastric biopsy

culture.media: Selective media such as Skirrow's agar, incubated in a microaerophilic atmosphere
culture.growthCharacteristics: Slow growing, microaerophilic — requires 5-10% O2 and added CO2
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, translucent colonies after several days of incubation

biochemicalTests.result: + — strongly positive; basis of the urea breath test and rapid urease test

identificationClues: Strongly urease positive — basis of the rapid urease test and urea breath test
Multiple polar flagella (flagellar tuft) giving corkscrew motility
Found on gastric biopsy in chronic gastritis or peptic ulcer disease

diseases: Peptic ulcer disease — gastric and duodenal ulcers
Increased risk of gastric adenocarcinoma and MALT lymphoma
virulenceFactors: Urease — neutralizes stomach acid locally, enabling survival
Flagella — motility through the mucus layer
CagA and VacA toxins — associated with more severe disease
clinicalImportance.transmission: Person to person, likely via fecal-oral or oral-oral routes; exact routes are not fully established
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common chronic bacterial infections worldwide; prevalence varies widely by region and socioeconomic factors
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Urease-based tests — rapid urease test, urea breath test, and stool antigen — are the mainstay of both invasive and non-invasive diagnosis

examFacts.importantDisease: Peptic ulcer disease; gastric adenocarcinoma risk
examFacts.importantTest: Urea breath test; rapid urease test on gastric biopsy
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Urease-producing, microaerophilic, helical Gram-negative rod that colonizes the stomach
